cards.name: Anterior division (branch) of retromandibular vein
cards.function: Anterior of the two terminal branches of the retromandibular vein; it carries blood from the superficial temporal and maxillary territories forward to the facial vein and so into the internal jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises where the retromandibular vein divides at the lower pole of the parotid gland, near the angle of the mandible

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward and downward below the angle of the mandible, superficial to the external carotid artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the facial vein to form the common facial vein, which ends in the internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerges from the lower pole of the parotid; lies near the marginal mandibular and cervical branches of the facial nerve and the submandibular gland

cards.pearl: The divisions decide where parotid and scalp blood ends up: anterior division to the internal jugular system, posterior division to the external jugular vein.

cards.name: Posterior division (branch) of retromandibular vein
cards.function: Posterior of the two terminal branches of the retromandibular vein; it unites with the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises where the retromandibular vein divides at the lower pole of the parotid gland, near the angle of the mandible

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes backward and downward from the parotid onto the surface of the sternocleidomastoid muscle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lower pole of the parotid gland, angle of the mandible, great auricular nerve on sternocleidomastoid

cards.name: Superior bulb of internal jugular vein
cards.function: Dilated beginning of the internal jugular vein in the jugular fossa, where it receives the sigmoid sinus; it lies directly beneath the floor of the middle ear.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of the sigmoid sinus at the jugular foramen; the inferior petrosal sinus joins at or just below it

details.label: Course
details.value: Occupies the jugular fossa of the temporal bone in the posterior part of the jugular foramen, then continues down as the internal jugular vein in the carotid sheath

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Floor of the tympanic cavity above; CN IX, X and XI leave the jugular foramen anteromedial to it; internal carotid artery in front

cards.pearl: A high or dehiscent jugular bulb appears as a blue mass behind the tympanic membrane and causes pulsatile tinnitus; glomus jugulare tumors arise in its wall and can produce jugular foramen syndrome (CN IX, X, XI palsies).

cards.name: Inferior bulb of internal jugular vein
cards.function: Dilation at the lower end of the internal jugular vein just above its union with the subclavian vein; a bicuspid valve above it limits reflux of blood toward the head.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Lower end of the internal jugular vein; the external jugular and vertebral veins end close by

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies deep to the interval between the sternal and clavicular heads of sternocleidomastoid (lesser supraclavicular fossa), behind the medial end of the clavicle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the subclavian vein at the venous angle to form the brachiocephalic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Common carotid artery and vagus nerve medial; cervical pleura and first part of the subclavian artery behind; thoracic duct (left) or right lymphatic duct enters at the angle

cards.pearl: Target of the low (central) approach to internal jugular catheterization between the two heads of sternocleidomastoid; the nearby pleura and, on the left, the thoracic duct are at risk.

cards.name: Superior labial vein
cards.function: Drains the upper lip and adjacent nasal septum and ala into the facial vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Venous network of the upper lip; communicates across the midline and with the external nasal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally in the upper lip with the superior labial artery, between orbicularis oris and the mucosa

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein near the angle of the mouth

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior labial artery, orbicularis oris, labial glands

cards.pearl: Lies in the danger triangle of the face: infection of the upper lip and nose can reach the cavernous sinus through the valveless facial, angular and ophthalmic veins.

cards.name: Inferior labial vein
cards.function: Drains the lower lip into the facial vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Venous network of the lower lip; communicates with the mental vein and the vein of the opposite side

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally in the lower lip with the inferior labial artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein below the angle of the mouth

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior labial artery, orbicularis oris, depressor anguli oris

cards.name: External palatine (paratonsillar) vein
cards.function: Drains the soft palate and the tonsillar bed downward across the lateral surface of the palatine tonsil to the facial vein or pharyngeal venous plexus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins of the soft palate and palatine tonsil

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends from the soft palate on the lateral surface of the tonsillar capsule, then pierces the superior pharyngeal constrictor

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein (or the pharyngeal venous plexus)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tonsillar bed (superior constrictor), palatine tonsil, tonsillar branch of the facial artery

cards.pearl: The usual source of venous bleeding after tonsillectomy, because it runs in the tonsillar bed just lateral to the capsule.

cards.name: Superior ophthalmic vein
cards.function: Main vein of the orbit: drains the eyeball, upper orbit and eyelids backward into the cavernous sinus and communicates in front with the angular vein, linking the face to the intracranial sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins at the medial angle of the orbit from the nasofrontal vein (from the supraorbital, supratrochlear and angular veins); receives the superior vorticose veins, central retinal vein, lacrimal and ethmoidal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward with the ophthalmic artery beneath the superior rectus, crosses above the optic nerve and leaves through the superior orbital fissure

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Valveless; passes through the superior orbital fissure outside (above) the common tendinous ring

cards.pearl: A dilated superior ophthalmic vein on CT or MRI with pulsatile proptosis, chemosis and an orbital bruit indicates a carotid-cavernous fistula; the vein also carries facial infection to the cavernous sinus.

cards.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein
cards.function: Drains the floor of the orbit, the inferior extraocular muscles and the lower part of the eyeball to the cavernous sinus, with a communication to the pterygoid venous plexus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Venous network on the floor and medial wall of the orbit; receives the inferior vorticose veins and veins of the inferior rectus, inferior oblique and lower eyelid

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward on the inferior rectus along the floor of the orbit

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus, directly or by joining the superior ophthalmic vein; a branch passes through the inferior orbital fissure to the pterygoid plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Valveless; inferior rectus, infraorbital vessels and nerve, inferior orbital fissure

cards.name: Central retinal vein
cards.function: Sole venous drainage of the inner retina: the retinal venules converge on the optic disc and leave the eye within the optic nerve.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior and inferior nasal, temporal and macular retinal venules, uniting at the optic disc

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs in the optic nerve alongside the central retinal artery, then leaves the nerve behind the eyeball and crosses the subarachnoid space

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior ophthalmic vein or directly into the cavernous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Central retinal artery within the optic nerve and lamina cribrosa of the sclera

cards.pearl: Central retinal vein occlusion causes sudden painless monocular vision loss with diffuse retinal hemorrhages, dilated tortuous veins and disc edema (blood and thunder fundus); raised intracranial pressure compresses the vein and abolishes venous pulsation, contributing to papilledema.

cards.name: Deep cervical vein
cards.function: Drains the suboccipital region and the deep muscles of the back of the neck, accompanying the deep cervical artery down to the vertebral vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus, occipital vein and veins of the deep posterior neck muscles; communicates with the venous plexus around the vertebral artery

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends between semispinalis capitis and semispinalis cervicis, then passes forward between the C7 transverse process and the neck of the first rib

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Lower end of the vertebral vein (or the brachiocephalic vein)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep cervical artery, semispinalis muscles, costocervical trunk

cards.name: Transverse sinus
cards.function: Paired dural sinus that carries blood from the confluence of sinuses laterally along the occipital bone to the sigmoid sinus; the right usually continues the superior sagittal sinus and the left the straight sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins at the confluence of sinuses; receives the superior petrosal sinus, inferior cerebral veins, inferior anastomotic vein (of Labbé), inferior cerebellar veins and diploic veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally and forward in the attached margin of the tentorium cerebelli, in the groove for the transverse sinus of the occipital bone, to the base of the petrous temporal bone

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Continues as the sigmoid sinus where the superior petrosal sinus joins

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli; occipital lobe above and cerebellum below; the right sinus is usually the larger

cards.pearl: Transverse sinus thrombosis (often from otitis media or mastoiditis, or in hypercoagulable states) presents with headache and papilledema and can cause temporal lobe venous infarction through the vein of Labbé; a hypoplastic left sinus is a common normal variant on MR venography.

cards.name: Sigmoid sinus
cards.function: S-shaped continuation of the transverse sinus that descends behind the mastoid to the jugular foramen, where it becomes the internal jugular vein; the final common pathway for most intracranial venous blood.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of the transverse sinus; receives the mastoid and condylar emissary veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Curves downward and medially in the sigmoid groove of the temporal and occipital bones, then turns forward to the posterior part of the jugular foramen

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior bulb of the internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Mastoid air cells and mastoid antrum laterally (thin plate of bone between); cerebellum medially; facial canal in front

cards.pearl: Mastoiditis or chronic otitis media can erode into the sinus and cause septic sigmoid (lateral) sinus thrombosis: spiking fevers, headache and edema over the mastoid from thrombosis of the mastoid emissary vein (Griesinger sign). The sinus is at risk in mastoidectomy.

cards.name: Parietal emissary vein
cards.function: Valveless vein passing through the parietal foramen to connect the veins of the scalp with the superior sagittal sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Scalp veins near the vertex (tributaries of the superficial temporal and occipital veins)

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the parietal foramen beside the sagittal suture, just in front of lambda

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus (flow may run in either direction)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Loose areolar tissue layer of the scalp, parietal bone, sagittal suture

cards.pearl: Scalp infection in the loose areolar (danger) layer can spread through it to the superior sagittal sinus, causing sinus thrombosis or meningitis.

cards.name: Mastoid emissary vein
cards.function: Valveless vein passing through the mastoid foramen to connect the sigmoid sinus with the veins behind the ear.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Sigmoid sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the mastoid foramen behind the mastoid process, accompanied by a meningeal branch of the occipital artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Posterior auricular vein or occipital vein (flow may run in either direction)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Mastoid process, occipitomastoid suture, occipital artery

cards.pearl: Edema and tenderness over the mastoid from thrombosis of this vein (Griesinger sign) points to septic sigmoid sinus thrombosis complicating mastoiditis; it bleeds briskly in retrosigmoid craniotomy.

cards.name: Occipital emissary vein
cards.function: Inconstant valveless vein through the occipital bone near the external occipital protuberance, connecting the confluence of sinuses with the occipital vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Confluence of sinuses; also receives the occipital diploic vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through a small foramen in the squamous part of the occipital bone at the external occipital protuberance

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Occipital vein (flow may run in either direction)

details.label: Relations
details.value: External occipital protuberance, occipital artery, greater occipital nerve

cards.name: Condylar emissary vein
cards.function: Inconstant valveless vein passing through the condylar canal to connect the sigmoid sinus with the suboccipital and vertebral venous plexuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Lower end of the sigmoid sinus (or superior bulb of the internal jugular vein)

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the condylar canal, which opens in the condylar fossa behind the occipital condyle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus, venous plexus around the vertebral artery and deep cervical vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Occipital condyle, atlantooccipital joint, vertebral artery; a meningeal branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery shares the canal

cards.pearl: Links the dural sinuses to the valveless vertebral venous plexus, an alternative outflow of the brain in the upright position and a route for spread of infection or tumor.

cards.name: Petrosal vein
cards.function: Short, large vein in the cerebellopontine angle that collects the veins of the pons and the anterior cerebellum and empties into the superior petrosal sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Transverse and lateral pontine veins, anterior pontomesencephalic vein, vein of the lateral recess of the 4th ventricle and cerebellar hemispheric veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward and laterally in the cerebellopontine angle cistern to the petrous ridge

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior petrosal sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Trigeminal nerve root just medial and below; facial and vestibulocochlear nerves behind; tentorium cerebelli above

cards.pearl: Encountered next to the trigeminal root in microvascular decompression for trigeminal neuralgia and in cerebellopontine angle surgery; sacrificing it can cause venous infarction of the cerebellum or brainstem.

cards.name: Inferior cerebral veins
cards.function: Superficial veins draining the inferior surface of the hemisphere and the lower lateral cortex into the dural sinuses at the base of the skull.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Cortical veins of the orbital surface of the frontal lobe and the inferior surfaces of the temporal and occipital lobes; lie beneath the arachnoid

details.label: Course
details.value: Run across the inferior surface of the hemisphere toward the nearest basal sinus

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Transverse, superior petrosal, cavernous and sphenoparietal sinuses; some join the basal vein (of Rosenthal) or the superficial middle cerebral vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli and floor of the anterior and middle cranial fossae

cards.name: Deep middle cerebral vein
cards.function: Drains the insula and the deep part of the lateral sulcus and is one of the roots of the basal vein (of Rosenthal).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Insular veins in the floor of the lateral (sylvian) sulcus

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs medially in the depth of the lateral sulcus with the middle cerebral artery to the anterior perforated substance

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the anterior cerebral vein and inferior thalamostriate veins to form the basal vein (of Rosenthal)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Insula, middle cerebral artery, optic tract and uncus

cards.name: Veins of posterior cranial fossa (cerebellar and brain stem veins)
cards.function: Veins of the cerebellum and brain stem, which leave the posterior fossa in three directions: upward to the great cerebral vein, forward to the petrosal vein and superior petrosal sinus, and backward to the straight and transverse sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Cortical veins of the cerebellar vermis and hemispheres and the surface veins of the midbrain, pons and medulla, continuous below with the anterior and posterior spinal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Lie on the surfaces of the cerebellum and brain stem in the subarachnoid cisterns; they do not follow the arteries

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Great cerebral vein (of Galen) and basal vein; petrosal vein to the superior petrosal sinus; straight sinus, transverse sinuses and confluence of sinuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli above, falx cerebelli and occipital sinus behind, cranial nerves V to XII in the cisterns

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior group (to the great cerebral vein and basal vein): precentral cerebellar vein, superior vermian vein with preculminate and intraculminate veins, superior cerebellar vein, posterior and lateral mesencephalic veins; anterior group (to the petrosal vein and superior petrosal sinus): anterior pontomesencephalic vein, transverse and lateral pontine veins, anteromedian medullary vein, vein of the lateral recess of the 4th ventricle; posterior group (to the straight and transverse sinuses): inferior vermian vein, inferior cerebellar hemispheric veins, superior and inferior retrotonsillar veins
